toc.title: The exam in one page, and pacing
Your final week and exam day

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Plan your time across the two halves
  • Read a stem and a scenario in a fixed order: the ask, the role, the instrument and the stage
  • Answer multi-select questions with exactly the right number of options
  • Match your answer to the depth that the verb asks for
  • Eliminate options that fall into the common traps
  • Prepare the final week and exam day, and know what happens afterwards

2The exam in one page, and pacing

The Exam in One Page [Verify live]

  • 100 items, all multiple choice, including case studies and scenarios; no essays; one point for each correct answer
  • 2.75 hours of testing time, with a 15-minute break halfway
  • Two halves: each holds half the questions and half the time, and the first half cannot be reopened after you submit it
  • Passing score: 300 on a scale of 100 to 500; passing takes a set number of correct answers, and section percentages cannot be averaged to find it
  • Scope: topics in the Body of Knowledge, but you may be asked to apply them to situations the materials do not show
  • As of 27 October 2026: confirm the format on IAPP's pages

Exam tip: Know the structure before test day, so that the only surprises are the questions.

Pacing: About Ninety-Nine Seconds a Question

  • Arithmetic: 165 minutes for 100 items is about 99 seconds an item
  • Each half: 50 questions in 82.5 minutes
  • Checkpoints: question 25 by about 41 minutes and question 50 by about 82 minutes; the same again in the second half
  • Bank time: short definition questions take less, scenarios take more
  • Cap a hard question: choose your best answer, flag it and move on
  • Use the break to reset, not to study

Exam tip: A hard question is worth the same single point as an easy one, so do not let it eat the clock.

3Answering the questions

Reading a Stem: Five Steps

  • Find the ask: the last sentence; words such as best, first, most likely change the answer
  • Read the facts: who is involved, which system, where and when
  • Mark the role, the instrument and the stage (next slide)
  • Predict an answer before you read the options
  • Match and eliminate: options are written to tempt, so compare each with your prediction
  • Skip nothing: a number, a region or a date in the stem is there for a reason

Exam tip: Predict the answer before you read the options, because the options are built to tempt.

Scenario Questions: Role, Instrument and Stage

  • A scenario is a bundle of facts: sort them before you read the options
  • Role decides whose duties apply (modules 2 and 6)
  • Instrument decides which rule applies (modules 4 to 7)
  • Stage decides which control fits (modules 8 to 13)
  • Distractors often give a right answer for the wrong role, instrument or stage
  • Do the sort every time, even when the answer looks obvious

Exam tip: Name the role, the instrument and the stage first: most wrong options fail one of the three.

Multi-Select: Exactly N, No Partial Credit

  • The stem says how many to select; select exactly that number
  • No partial credit: one wrong choice, or one missing, scores nothing
  • Judge each option on its own as true or false for this stem, then count the trues
  • More trues than the number asked for? Re-read the stem for the qualifier: first, best, most
  • Fewer? Re-check the options you marked false: one may be right in this context
  • Watch for options that are true in general but do not answer this stem

Exam tip: Treat each option as its own true-or-false question, then count.

The Verbs Set the Depth: How to Answer

  • Module 0: the verb that starts an indicator sets the depth of the question
  • Understand, identify: the correct statement, or the term that fits
  • Apply, conduct, perform: the best action in the situation
  • Evaluate, assess: the best-justified judgment
  • Create, establish: the policy or control that must exist
  • Two options both true? Pick the one that fits the depth of the verb

Exam tip: Ask what the question wants you to do with the knowledge: recall it, choose with it, judge with it or build with it.

Eliminating Options: Traps That Look Right

  • Absolute words: always, never, only and all are rarely true in governance
  • Wrong role: a provider duty handed to the deployer, or the reverse
  • Wrong stage: a monitoring fix for a design problem
  • Wrong instrument: a GDPR rule for an AI Act question
  • True but off-question: a correct fact that does not answer this stem
  • Skipped step: going live before the assessment, or acting before containing the harm

Exam tip: Strike the options that fail on role, instrument or stage; what is left is usually the answer.

Flagging, Changing Answers and the First-Half Rule

  • Use flags for questions you want to revisit within a half; the forward and backward arrows move between questions
  • The first half is final: after you submit it you cannot return, so clear your flags before you submit
  • Answer every question: each correct answer earns a point, and a blank cannot
  • Change an answer only for a reason: a fact you recalled or a qualifier you missed, not a feeling
  • Keep a few minutes at the end of each half for flagged items
  • Do not carry doubt into the second half

Exam tip: Because the first half cannot be reopened, finish and review it before you submit.

Look-Alike Pairs the Course Teaches Apart

  • DPIA and FRIA: personal data rights under the GDPR; fundamental rights by certain deployers under the AI Act
  • Provider and deployer; controller and processor: who builds or decides, and who uses or acts on behalf
  • Red teaming, audit, threat modeling: try to break it, check compliance, map attack paths
  • Incident, issue, risk: it happened and harmed, a problem was found, it may happen
  • Deactivate and localize; NIST, ISO and OECD: off or limited; framework, certifiable standard, principles

Exam tip: When two options differ by one of these pairs, check the stem for which side applies.

4Your final week and exam day

Your Final Week: A Plan

  • IAPP recommends at least 30 hours of study in total; the final week consolidates
  • Study materials are tools, not a one-to-one guide to exam content
  • Practice in halves: 50 questions in 82.5 minutes
  • Sort your misses by cause: role, instrument, stage, verb or a missed qualifier
  • Recheck the pages tagged Dates and Verify live
  • Light last day: logistics and sleep, not new topics

Exam tip: Fix the cause of each miss, not only the answer.

Exam Day at a Test Center [Verify live]

  • Arrive 15 minutes early; a late arrival may be treated as a no-show, and all fees are forfeited
  • Bring two qualifying forms of ID that meet the test center's requirements
  • No electronic devices and no reading material in the exam room
  • The timer does not stop if you leave the room for a break
  • Reschedule or cancel up to 48 hours before the appointment, and wait for the confirmation email
  • Special accommodations: ask as early as you can
  • As of 27 October 2026: the rules are in the handbook version in force, so check it before you book

Exam tip: Do the logistics a week early: ID, route and timing should be boring on the day.

Exam Day Online With OnVUE [Verify live]

  • Use a personal computer, not a work-issued one, with no virtual private network (VPN); run the system check on the microphone, webcam and internet speed
  • Check-in opens 30 minutes before; you photograph yourself, a government-issued ID and four views of your surroundings
  • Rules: keep your face in view, stay at your workspace, nobody else in the room, no headphones, one beverage only, no speaking aloud
  • Proctoring: a human proctor watches by webcam and microphone; AI assists, and a person makes the decisions
  • Change or cancel the appointment until 15 minutes after the scheduled start
  • As of 27 October 2026: confirm the rules on the handbook and Pearson VUE pages

Exam tip: Test your setup well before exam day, and clear the room of anything that looks like study material.

After the Exam: Results, Breakdown and Next Steps [Verify live]

  • Results are immediate: pass or fail, and the score
  • A later email gives a breakdown by section; IAPP does not give the number of correct answers
  • If you do not pass: a retake no sooner than 7 days after the attempt, at a discounted price; use the section breakdown to aim your study
  • If you pass: certification maintenance is USD 250 for a two-year term, or IAPP membership at USD 295 a year, plus 20 credits a year
  • Exams are updated each year, about 10% to 15% of content, announced at least 90 days ahead
  • As of 27 October 2026: confirm fees and rules on IAPP's site

Exam tip: A section breakdown is a map of where to study, not a verdict on you.

5Final Checklist

  • Technique: 99 seconds a question; checkpoints at 25 and 50; find the ask; role, instrument, stage; predict, then match; exactly N for multi-select
  • Traps: absolutes, wrong role, wrong stage, wrong instrument, true but off-question, skipped step
  • First half: flag, review and clear it before you submit
  • Review: recap pages, glossary, look-alike pairs, and the Dates and Verify live pages
  • Logistics: ID, route or room, system check, confirmation email, sleep
  • Mindset: every question is one point; take the next one

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (one best answer, or select exactly the number the question asks for)

Running case

The Helios Candidate Chat

  • Helios plans a candidate chat: job applicants in the EU and in New York City ask about roles and the hiring process, and can ask it to summarize their own résumé
  • It runs on the general-purpose model from Corvid Labs, used through an interface and grounded on Helios's careers pages
  • Anika Berg's team wants to launch in six weeks
  • Jonas Weber notes that the chat will process applicants' personal data
  • Mei Tanaka notes that it will accept free-text input from anyone
  • Samira Haddad asks the governance lead for a recommendation before the launch decision
  • Five questions follow: answer each one from the case, using role, instrument and stage

S1In the Helios candidate chat case, which describes Helios's role for the chat?

  • AThe provider of the chat offered under its own name, and a deployer of the Corvid Labs model
  • BOnly a deployer, because the model comes from Corvid Labs and Helios builds nothing of its own to offer applicants
  • CA distributor, because the chat passes the model's answers on to applicants without changing them
  • DA controller, so that no AI Act role applies to the chat, whatever it does
Show the answer

Answer: A. Helios builds the chat on the model and offers it under its own name, so it is the provider of the chat, and it also deploys the Corvid Labs model. A feature built on a model does not make Helios a mere distributor, and a controller can also hold AI Act roles.

S2In the Helios candidate chat case, which TWO checks should the governance lead make first? (Select TWO.)

  • AWhether the GDPR applies, because the chat will process applicants' personal data
  • BWhether the chat is a medical device, because an applicant might ask about health-related adjustments
  • CWhether the chat must follow vehicle type-approval rules, because some of the roles involve driving
  • DWhether the chat falls under the rules for nuclear installations, because one office is near such a site
  • EWhether the AI Act's transparency duties apply, because people will be interacting with an AI system
Show the answer

Answer: A, E. Personal data brings the GDPR, and a system that interacts with people brings the AI Act's transparency duties under Article 50. Medical device, vehicle and nuclear rules have nothing to do with a careers chat.

S3The Helios team wants to launch the candidate chat in six weeks. Which activity belongs at the decision-to-deploy stage and should be finished before launch?

  • AReading the first month's usage logs to see what applicants asked the chat once it was live
  • BPublishing a public statement about a data leak that was found some time after the launch
  • CAn impact assessment of the selected chat, with the provider's documents and Helios's tests
  • DRetiring the chat and deleting its records once the hiring season has ended
Show the answer

Answer: C. Before go-live the deployer assesses the system it chose, with the provider's documents and its own tests. Reading logs and answering a leak come after launch, and retirement comes at the end of the life cycle.

S4During testing of the candidate chat, a tester types hidden instructions into the free-text box and the chat reveals part of its configuration. Which risk is this, and what is the best next step?

  • APrompt injection: add input and output controls and limits on what the chat can reveal or do, then retest
  • BData drift: retrain the model on a new set of applicants' questions and release it straight away, without testing
  • CModel theft: switch the chat off in each region and abandon the project
  • DBias in selection rates: calculate the impact ratio for each group of applicants who used the chat
Show the answer

Answer: A. Hidden instructions in input that change the system's behavior are prompt injection. Add controls on inputs, outputs and permissions, and retest with red teaming. Drift, model theft and selection-rate bias are different problems.

S5Weeks after launch, the candidate chat gives applicants visa-sponsorship details taken from an outdated careers page. What is the best response?

  • AWait to see whether applicants complain before taking action on the matter
  • BRetrain the underlying model from scratch on the corrected page and release it straight away, without testing it
  • CDelete the logs of the affected conversations, so that the error is harder to trace
  • DContain the harm, log the incident, fix the source and retest, and tell those affected as required
Show the answer

Answer: D. The cause is a stale document in the retrieval source, so contain the harm, record the incident, fix the document and its ownership, retest and communicate. Waiting, retraining the whole model and deleting evidence make things worse.
